Claudĭŏpŏlis , is; acc. im; abl. i, f.
I. A town in Southern Cappadocia, now Eraklia, Plin. 5, 24, 20, § 85; Amm. 14, 8, 2.—
II. A town in Bithynia, prob. the mod. Boli or Bula, Cod. Th. 12, 1, 119.—Hence, Claudĭŏpŏlītāni , ōrum, m., the inhabitants of Claudiopolis in Bithynia, Plin. Ep. 10, 39 (48), 5; Traj. ib. 10, 40 (49), 3.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
